clue.text: Scattered boxes close to store

parts.note: to box in training is to spar, so 'boxes' gives spars

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so its final letter is taken

explanation.surface: Someone describes packing boxes left lying about near a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxes' looks like a noun but is the verb: a boxer spars.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something thinly distributed or few and far between is scattered.

clue.text: Is coming over about affected seafood

indicators.note: about means the turned pair goes round the next piece
in a down clue a word coming over is flipped upward, so these two letters are read backwards

parts.note: camp means affected or exaggerated in manner

explanation.surface: A pretentious diner's prawn dish arrives at the table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming over' turns the two-letter word upward to SI; 'about' then wraps that pair round the word for affected.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: breaded langoustine tails are a familiar dish of shellfish served in British pubs.

clue.text: County town may be busy early, surprisingly

indicators.note: surprisingly signals the letters fall into an unexpected new order

explanation.surface: A market town might be crowded first thing in the morning, unexpectedly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprisingly' rearranges BUSYEARLY; 'may be' is a link. The answer is the county town of Buckinghamshire, an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: this Buckinghamshire town is the administrative centre of its county.

clue.text: Completely intoxicated son's given ground

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for son
ground, as of potatoes or grain, means crushed or mashed

explanation.surface: A drunken son has been knocked to the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' reads as the floor but is the past participle of grind.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang synonym: very drunk people are often described as blotto or wasted, and this word means the same.

clue.text: Weapon-holder in small taxi, driven initially round block

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a cab is a taxi
to bar is to block

indicators.note: initially means only the first letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: A sword sheath travels in a little cab, driven round the block.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' is loose: the first letter of 'driven' comes round to follow the block word rather than precede it, as the clue order suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a sheath for a sword or dagger is literally the holder of a blade weapon.

clue.text: Cheerfulness shown by soldiers after short time under canvas below bluff

indicators.note: below places the canvas piece beneath the bluff in this down entry
under places the soldiers beneath the canvas piece in this down entry

parts.note: a con is a bluff or deception
a tent is made of canvas, so under canvas means in a tent
men is a common crossword term for soldiers
T is an abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Troops are happy after a brief spell camping beneath a cliff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bluff' looks like a cliff but means deception. 'after' loosely links MEN and T.
explanation.definitionFit: Near-synonym: a state of satisfied happiness shades into cheerfulness.

clue.text: US actor and actress Eleanor accompanying boy

parts.note: Eleanor Bron is a British actress
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A Hollywood star appears with a British actress and a young lad.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Bronson was the American star of Death Wish.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Charles Bronson was a tough-guy Hollywood film star.

clue.text: Professional wearing article, protective garment

indicators.note: the professional is wearing the article, so it sits inside that word

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
pro is short for professional

explanation.surface: An expert puts on a piece of protective clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a pinafore worn by cooks keeps food off their clothes.

clue.text: Groom ahead of time in equestrian event

indicators.note: ahead of places the groom piece first, above the time piece

parts.note: to groom is to dress or tidy
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A stable hand gets a horse ready before the show starts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Groom' suggests a stable hand, but here it means dress.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an Olympic horse-riding discipline where trained movements are judged.

clue.text: At sea in a launch

parts.note: to launch a company is to float it on the stock market

explanation.surface: A boat being launched is out on the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'launch' suggests a boat, but here it is floating a company.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a ship on the water and not sunk is buoyant and out at sea.

clue.text: Where a golfer may be seen heading in the right direction

definitions.text: Where a golfer may be seen
definitions.meaning: a golfer is out playing the links, on the playing ground
making progress as planned, like a ship keeping to its route

explanation.surface: A golfer seen walking the right way round the links.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom plus literal sense: on track, and literally on the golf ground.

clue.text: Quickly pass to the suspect

indicators.note: suspect as an adjective means dodgy, so the letters are unreliable and reshuffled

explanation.surface: Hurry and pass the ball to the person under suspicion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspect' reads as a noun but is an adjective signalling rearrangement of PASSTOTHE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an old phrase for with all speed, from messengers rushing the mail.

clue.text: Pull out queen, say — this may win you instant cash

definitions.text: this may win you instant cash

parts.note: to scratch is to withdraw from a race or contest
a queen is an example of a playing card

explanation.surface: A gambler withdraws a queen from the deck hoping for a quick win.
explanation.walkthrough: 'queen, say' indicates an example, a playing card.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a lottery ticket whose covered panels you rub to reveal an immediate prize.

clue.text: Conveys object on board steamship

indicators.note: on board means carried inside the ship, so a word sits between its letters

parts.note: an end is an aim or object

explanation.surface: A ship carries cargo aboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: dispatches or transmits something to another place.

clue.text: Getting beneath station

parts.note: under means beneath
station means rank or social standing

explanation.surface: Going down under a railway station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'station' means social rank, not a railway stop.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang synonym: to get a joke is to grasp or comprehend it.

clue.text: Beer, for example, at inn — 'bier' abroad

indicators.note: abroad means scattered widely, so the letters are spread into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Beer at a pub, and a coffin stand, in a foreign tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abroad' suggests a foreign language (Bier is German for beer) but rearranges ATINNBIER.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: any alcoholic drink, beer included, is an intoxicant.

clue.text: Old boy's story about opening of cocktail bar

parts.note: OB is short for old boy, a former pupil

indicators.note: about means the story wraps round the next letter

parts.note: a tale is a story

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A former pupil tells an anecdote about a cocktail bar opening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a pub but is the definition: a barrier.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a barrier or hindrance blocks the way.

clue.text: Telephoned by a drunk? That's unacceptable

indicators.note: drunk means the letters are staggering about in disorder

explanation.surface: Getting a phone call from an inebriate is out of order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges TELEPHONEDBYA.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: outside the bounds of acceptable behaviour, from the old fenced boundary round Dublin.

clue.text: Budding number on climb

indicators.note: on in a down clue places the first piece above the second

parts.note: an ascent is a climb

explanation.surface: A young plant counts its climb.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: just coming into being, beginning to develop.

clue.text: Girl ringing home for forgiveness

indicators.note: ringing means surrounding, so the girl goes round the home

parts.note: Amy is a girl's name
a nest is a home

explanation.surface: A girl telephones home to ask to be forgiven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ringing' suggests phoning, but means encircling.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an official pardon granted for offences.

clue.text: Queen describing former extension

indicators.note: describing means drawing round, so the queen encircles the next piece

parts.note: Anne was a British queen
ex means former

explanation.surface: A queen talks about a former building extension.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describing' is used in its geometric sense of drawing a line round.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an added building or wing attached to a main one.

clue.text: Squabbles caused by dogs mother's abandoned

indicators.note: abandoned means mother's letters are left out of the dogs

parts.note: mastiffs are a breed of large dog
ma is mother, and the possessive adds an S

explanation.surface: Quarrels start because Mum's dogs have been left behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: petty quarrels or minor disagreements.

clue.text: River, south-eastern? Wrong

parts.note: the Fal is a river in Cornwall

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a river is in the south-east and is told no.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: untrue or incorrect.

clue.text: Success with single is a sort of accident

parts.note: a hit is a success
and means with or plus
a single is one run in cricket

explanation.surface: A cricketer's lucky shot and quick run cause a mishap.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a single is one run scored.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a road collision where the driver leaves the scene.

clue.text: 'Blind alley', possibly clued as 'Close', originally

indicators.note: possibly means the letters could be arranged otherwise
originally means the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A puzzle setter discusses defining a dead end with the word Close.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges CLUEDAS; Close is also a name for such a street.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a street closed at one end is a dead end, French for bottom of the bag.

clue.text: English country manor

parts.note: a state is a country

explanation.surface: A typical English country house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'country' looks like an adjective but is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a landed property with a large house.

clue.text: What may be evident to east in the latter part of the day?

definitions.text: the latter part of the day

indicators.note: may be suggests these letters could form something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: A puzzle about what is obvious towards the east at dusk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be' rearranges EVIDENT plus E.
explanation.definitionFit: Poetic synonym: evening, an old literary word for dusk.

clue.text: Evergreen tree with crack in it, set back

indicators.note: set back means the whole is written backwards
in it means the attempt goes inside the tree

parts.note: an elm is a tree
to have a crack is to have a try

explanation.surface: A tree whose trunk has split is pushed back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in it' puts the attempt inside the tree, making ELTRYM, which 'set back' then turns round; 'it' refers back to the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a shrub with glossy leaves that keeps them all year.
